observation_summary: The StrBuilder.contains(char) and indexOf(char) methods fail because they iterate up to the buffer's physical capacity (thisBuf.length) rather than the logical size of the string stored in the builder (size).
hypothesis: The methods incorrectly use the internal buffer's total length as the loop boundary condition instead of the current logical size of the StrBuilder, causing the methods to scan stale data beyond the end of the valid string.
prediction: The code will show a loop condition or boundary check using 'thisBuf.length' that should be replaced with 'this.size'.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly states that 'thisBuf.length' is used where 'size' should be used, and the test failure confirms that the method is looking beyond the end of the string.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic boundary condition error where the loop termination logic is incorrect. It is not an algorithmic rewrite (the search logic is fine, just the range is wrong) nor an initialization error. It fits the 'Checking' category as it involves an incorrect boundary check in a loop.
evidence_used: Bug report description: 'StrBuilder contains usages of thisBuf.length when they should use size'
Test failure: 'The contains(char) method is looking beyond the end of the string'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the loop logic is part of the method, the root cause is specifically the incorrect boundary condition (the check), which is the hallmark of a Checking defect.
